sections.h2: Why Do Qatar Businesses Choose ERPNext?

paragraphs.text: ERPNext is an open-source ERP with no licence fee per user, covering accounts, stock, buying, selling, projects, manufacturing and HR in one system. That suits Qatar's contracting, facility management and trading companies, which often need project costing, multi-currency buying and large payrolls in one place. A typical Qatar implementation takes 8–12 weeks for a single company.

As an ERPNext implementation company Qatar firms can work with remotely or on site, we plan each project around your tax year, payroll cycle and largest customers. Our ERPNext implementation Qatar projects begin with a workshop on how your business actually runs.

sections.h2: Qatar Tax Rules and Your ERPNext Setup
sections.intro: Qatar has not introduced VAT, but businesses still have tax records to keep:

items.text: Corporate income tax applies to the share of profits owned by foreign shareholders, while Qatari and GCC-owned shares are generally exempt
Withholding tax applies to certain payments to non-resident service providers, such as royalties, technical fees and commissions
Tax returns and audited accounts must be supported by clean, traceable records
Large multinational groups may also fall under the global minimum tax rules

outro.html: ERPNext corporate tax Qatar setups tag ownership, withholding tax on supplier payments and related-party transactions, so your adviser can prepare returns from clean data. Always confirm current rules with the General Tax Authority or your tax adviser.

paragraphs.text: On 6 May 2026, Qatar's Cabinet approved a draft e-invoicing law and its executive regulations. Detailed requirements and dates have not yet been published, but a phased rollout is expected. Businesses that clean their customer data, standardise invoice fields and run on a system that can connect to a national platform will move fastest. Credit notes, debit notes and invoice numbering rules are likely to matter too, so we set these up consistently from the start. An ERPNext implementation company Qatar clients hire now should build with this in mind, and we do.

paragraphs.html: Qatar's Wage Protection System requires salaries to be paid through banks with a salary file. ERPNext's HR app handles attendance, leave, overtime and salary components, then produces the WPS file your bank needs. End-of-service gratuity is calculated under Qatar's labour law, which sets a minimum of three weeks' basic wage for each year of service. Annual leave, sick leave and unpaid leave are tracked per employee, and air ticket entitlements can be accrued monthly so the cost appears in the right period. Visa, Qatar ID and passport expiry dates trigger reminders well before renewal is due. For the full setup, see ERPNext HR and payroll for the GCC.

paragraphs.text: ERPNext for Qatar contractors relies on project costing and retention tracking. ERPNext job costing Qatar setups show profit per project before you invoice. ERPNext for Qatar traders focuses on landed cost and stock control. Our ERPNext solutions Qatar clients all use the same core system, configured for their sector.

Facility management is one of Qatar's largest service sectors, and it is hard to run on spreadsheets. ERPNext tracks each service contract, its sites, its staff and its recurring invoices. Technicians log visits and materials used, managers see cost and margin per contract, and invoices go out automatically each month. Many FM firms also need manpower supply contracts billed by hours worked, which ERPNext handles with timesheets. An ERPNext implementation company Qatar FM firms hire should understand both service contracts and large payrolls, because the two drive profit together.

ERPNext Qatar riyal accounting keeps every report in QAR, while purchases in USD, EUR, AED or INR post at the correct exchange rate. Exchange gains and losses are calculated automatically when payments are made, so your books stay accurate without manual adjustments. Bank accounts in different currencies can be reconciled inside ERPNext, and month-end revaluation of foreign balances runs in a few clicks.

Government buyers, banks and many customers expect Arabic, so any ERPNext implementation company Qatar businesses shortlist should design these documents early. ERPNext Arabic documents Qatar setups include bilingual invoices, quotations, delivery notes and statements, with Arabic laid out from right to left.

paragraphs.html: Most Qatar clients come from Tally, QuickBooks or spreadsheets. We move customers, suppliers, items, opening balances and open invoices, and your old system stays live until the trial balance matches. An ERPNext implementation company Qatar finance teams trust should finish every migration with a signed balance check. See ERPNext data migration.

items.q: Can ERPNext handle WPS salary files?
items.a: Yes. ERPNext's HR app calculates salaries and produces the WPS file your bank needs. We set up salary components, allowances and deductions, then test a full payroll run before go-live.
Not yet. Qatar has not introduced VAT, so ERPNext is set up without VAT templates. If VAT is introduced later, ERPNext can add it without a new system.

items.q: Is ERPNext ready for Qatar e-invoicing?
items.a: The detailed rules have not been published yet. ERPNext already produces structured invoice data and connects to e-invoicing platforms in other Gulf countries, so it is well placed to adapt once Qatar's requirements are released.

items.q: How long does an ERPNext project take in Qatar?
items.a: A single company usually goes live in 8–12 weeks. Contractors with many active projects take 12–14 weeks. A good ERPNext implementation company Qatar clients hire will give these dates in writing.

items.q: What does an ERPNext project cost in Qatar?
items.a: The price depends on users, companies, modules and payroll size. ERPNext itself has no licence fee. After a short discovery call, an ERPNext implementation company Qatar clients can trust should send a fixed quote with every line item, and ours does.
